reason_no_browser_timing: Exact browser timing was not available through the connected GitHub toolchain, so no synthetic millisecond claims are made.

loader.assembly: responses joined into one HTML string
loader.implication: Network fetches are parallel, but parsing/execution/rendering begins only after all payload parts complete and the monolithic document is written.

structural_findings: Startup is all-or-nothing: no meaningful first UI can render before all 16 payload files finish downloading.
The largest two payloads account for roughly two thirds of the transferred source, so splitting into 16 files does not by itself produce progressive rendering.
document.write of the concatenated payload forces a second full document parse after the loader page has already loaded.
The frozen payload contains extensive layered bootstrap/health/audit code and historical compatibility overrides; even when functionally safe, they increase parse and execution work at startup.
cache:no-store prevents normal browser reuse of payload responses between visits, increasing repeated-load cost.
likely_bottleneck_order: Network transfer, especially on cold/mobile connections
not_proven: Exact contribution in milliseconds of network versus JavaScript versus rendering
Whether cache:no-store alone explains any specific observed 15-second load
recommended_post_oos_sequence: Instrument real browser milestones: loader start, all payload fetched, document.write start/end, DOMContentLoaded, first useful dashboard paint, stableModelRefresh completion.
Remove cache:no-store or replace it with versioned immutable payload URLs so unchanged payload can be cached safely.
Make the initial shell and first selected view render before non-visible modules/audits are loaded.
Consolidate legacy override layers and duplicate bootstrap wrappers identified by the UI structure audit.
Reduce or lazy-load historical/diagnostic material not needed for first paint.
Re-measure on desktop and mobile before further optimization.

oos_safety.rule: Do not implement startup architecture changes before the active 1W OOS checkpoint unless a new OOS baseline is deliberately accepted.
